segments.cap: Sometimes the value you need has no tag and no field name. It sits inside a sentence, like a prerequisite inside a course description. A selector cannot reach it. A language model can.
With the ellmer package, we start a chat with chat_openai(). Then chat structured takes two things: the text, and a description of what we want back.
That description is type object, with one entry per column. Each entry has a type, such as type string, and a description. The description is your instruction to the model, so write it carefully.

What comes back has exactly those fields. That is all it guarantees. A schema fixes the shape of the answer, not its correctness. The same code can return different text on a second run, and each run costs money.
So check a sample against the page. And if a selector, or one line of code, can do the job, use that instead.
